items.excerpt: Josh King was always one of the best players in his age group. "Nationally," clarifies Charlie Turnbull, his coach in Fulham's academy for five seasons between his U10 and U14 years, to Sky Sports . But there was another quality that set hi…
body: Josh King was always one of the best players in his age group. "Nationally," clarifies Charlie Turnbull, his coach in Fulham's academy for five seasons between his U10 and U14 years, to Sky Sports . But there was another quality that set him apart.

"One of the most outstanding things about Josh is that whenever the level went up, whenever there was a pressure game, he loved it," adds Turnbull. "He loved it when things got hard. He loved it when there was a little bit of extra pressure.

"He wanted it. He wanted to feel like the pressure was on him and the responsibility was on him to produce for the team. He enjoyed that. You always saw the best of Josh when the ante was up. I never once saw him not deliver in those circumstances.

"We would play tournaments in France, Spain and Portugal, against the giants of Europe, and afterwards the staff from each club would have to pick the best player they'd seen across the weekend. I remember Josh winning that accolade more than once."

items.title: Kane targets biggest team prizes ahead of record-breaking England cap
items.excerpt: Harry Kane will become England's record appearance maker on Thursday night - but the Ballon d'Or winner now has his sights set on the biggest team trophies in football.
body: Harry Kane will become England's record appearance maker on Thursday night - but the Ballon d'Or winner now has his sights set on the biggest team trophies in football.
England captain Kane will win his 126th cap for his country against Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley. The landmark moment comes just weeks after he was crowned the best player in the world.

But while the striker has ended his long wait for team glory with back-to-back Bundesliga titles at Bayern Munich, as well as a German Cup, he is now eager to kick on again and land the most prestigious prizes for club and country.

"To win a team trophy with England, a major trophy, is my biggest dream," he said in a press conference on Wednesday when asked what comes next for him. "That's always been my biggest dream, to win a European Championship or a World Cup, or both, hopefully, but I know how difficult that is. Extremely motivated to do that.

items.title: Man Utd's Pochettino pursuit comes full circle - but would it work?
items.excerpt: Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United have a well-established history. One where paths might have crossed long before now, numerous times, but somehow never managed to converge.
body: Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United have a well-established history. One where paths might have crossed long before now, numerous times, but somehow never managed to converge.
Could it be that we are finally to bear witness to the culmination of this elaborate 10-year dance of incompatible circumstances?

The Old Trafford hierarchy have always admired Pochettino from afar. He was on their radar while at Tottenham and again when it was clear his time at PSG was coming to an end. The Argentine was eventually lured back to the Premier League, but instead returned to London, signing with Chelsea.

All along this journey of complicated courtship United were at play. There have been many sliding doors moments. At the time news broke of Chelsea's interest in Pochettino in 2023, United, coached by Erik ten Hag, had just been ripped to shreds by Sevilla. items.title: Sky pledges backing for Equal Sport Project
items.excerpt: Sky Sports is proud to support Equal Sport Project, which aims to accelerate progress towards equality across sport through five shared ambitions.
body: Sky Sports is proud to support Equal Sport Project, which aims to accelerate progress towards equality across sport through five shared ambitions.

The Equal Sport Project unites sport in the UK behind five shared ambitions for women and men across sport - from local leisure centres to the biggest stadiums, and from grassroots pitches to boardrooms.

Major sporting organisations from across the UK's sporting landscape - including the FA, RFU, Youth Sport Trust, England Netball, UK Sport, LTA, Women's Sport Trust, Women in Sport, Team GB and Sport England - have made specific pledges to drive progress and help turn these ambitions into reality. Brands and broadcasters are also playing their part, signalling growing support for the movement across the wider sporting industry.
The rest of the industry is also being asked to commit support and pledges as the project seeks to gain momentum in the months and years to come.

body: Scott McTominay has revealed he needed to have his heart “shocked” two days before Scotland's World Cup opener against Haiti.

The Napoli midfielder underwent a cardiac ablation procedure in Manchester in September to treat a mild, benign heart arrhythmia that first came to light after the Scots arrived in the United States in early June and then continued to affect him in August while back in Italy playing for his club.

At the time, the Scotland camp, clearly keen to keep McTominay's situation under wraps, said the 29-year-old had missed training in the lead-up to the World Cup due to a stomach complaint. items.title: Jobe joins brother Jude with England to showcase his own talent
items.excerpt: "He's coming on his own merit," said Thomas Tuchel, after extolling the strengths of Jobe Bellingham.
body: "He's coming on his own merit," said Thomas Tuchel, after extolling the strengths of Jobe Bellingham.

Jude Bellingham's younger brother - as is currently the go-to preface to any description of Jobe - couldn't hide his delight when he got the call from Tuchel to say he was being promoted from U21s captain to be included in the England senior squad.

"It's an incredible achievement for the family, for both brothers to be called up by their national team," Tuchel said on Friday, after revealing his squad for the Nations League games with Croatia and Spain. "I saw his excitement straightaway in his smile."

But Tuchel was also right to highlight the individual qualities of 21-year-old Jobe and the different attributes he can offer the national team, in a different position to his brother.
